system_description.narrative_title: Global political volatility: protests, election upsets and market shock
system_description.narrative_summary: Mass protests and surprising electoral upsets across multiple countries are interacting with investor panic and forceful state responses, producing cascading political and market volatility. As an open system, social mobilization, electoral dynamics and financial markets exchange information and resources with feedback loops (protests depress markets; market turmoil constrains policy options; electoral shocks reshape coalitions), while being driven by external inputs such as geopolitical alignments, media amplification and economic signals. Small triggers (violent incidents, narrow vote swings, judicial or administrative interventions) propagate rapidly through these linked domains and magnify systemic instability.
system_description.scope: Domestic political unrest, protest movements, electoral outcomes, investor reactions and state responses in affected countries (notably France, Brazil, Serbia, Israel and allied states) during the 25–27 Oct 2026 window; includes media and public sentiment that mediate interactions.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economic order (international capital markets, geopolitical rivalries, transnational media and diplomatic networks).
adjacent_subsystems: Media and social network information flows

variables.name: Social mobilization capacity
variables.description: The latent capacity of populations to organize collective action measured by network density, mobilization resources and readiness to protest.

variables.name: Protest event rate
variables.description: The frequency of organized public demonstrations and gatherings per unit time across the system.

variables.name: Protest violence rate
variables.description: The rate at which protests escalate into violent confrontations, measured by incidents involving physical force, property damage or clashes with security forces per unit time.

variables.name: Electoral volatility
variables.description: The degree of unpredictability and magnitude of swings in voting outcomes and party support between electoral cycles.

variables.name: Voter turnout momentum
variables.description: The rate of change in voter participation levels over short political cycles or campaign phases.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The prevailing level of risk sensitivity among investors reflected in preference shifts away from risky assets and expectations of future loss.

variables.name: Capital outflow rate
variables.description: The speed and volume at which financial capital is withdrawn from affected markets or jurisdictions per unit time.

variables.name: Asset price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and persistence of short-term fluctuations in asset prices and exchange rates within financial markets.

variables.name: Policy response forcefulness
variables.description: The intensity and coerciveness of state policy actions and enforcement measures deployed in response to unrest or instability.

variables.name: Fiscal policy space
variables.description: The available budgetary and fiscal capacity to deploy spending, transfers or stimulus without breaching sustainability constraints.

variables.name: Coalition stability
variables.description: The resilience and cohesiveness of governing alliances and political coalitions measured by turnover risk and internal disagreement pressures.

variables.name: Public trust in institutions
variables.description: The aggregate level of citizen confidence in political and administrative institutions and their perceived legitimacy.

variables.name: Media amplification
variables.description: The degree to which traditional and social media magnify, frame and spread political events and narratives across audiences.

variables.name: Judicial intervention rate
variables.description: The frequency of legal, judicial or administrative actions that affect electoral processes, protests or political actors per unit time.

variables.name: Contagion susceptibility
variables.description: The propensity for unrest, political shocks or market stress to spread across regions, sectors or countries given existing linkages.

variables.name: Security incident rate
variables.description: The occurrence rate of acute security-triggering events (eg. attacks, shootings, mass arrests) that can act as sudden catalysts for unrest.

catalysts.title: Continued mass protests in France
catalysts.description: Sustained waves of demonstrations and student-led actions demanding concessions, with repeated clashes in Paris and other cities.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hundreds of Thousands Protest Across France', 'French students vow more protests despite Macron government's concessions', 'Violence flares in Paris'.

catalysts.title: Push to pass anti-riot / 'make rioters pay' measures
catalysts.description: Government moves to tighten penalties and forceful measures against rioters, provoking criticism and likely legal and street responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Critics attack 'anti-democratic' French bill making rioters pay' and 'Macron promises "strong measures"'.

catalysts.title: Brazil market turmoil and fiscal reckoning
catalysts.description: Post-election selloff, currency plunge and investor repricing create sustained market volatility and constrain fiscal options for the incoming government.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Brazil’s currency tumbles', 'Brazilian Markets Crash After Lula’s Surprise Election Win', 'Lula faces a fiscal reckoning'.

catalysts.title: Bolsonaro-run legal challenge to Brazil vote
catalysts.description: Efforts by Bolsonaro and allies to annul or contest the election outcome through courts and administrative channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Bolsonaro refuses to concede, says he will seek annulment of Brazil vote', 'Trump says Brazil election looked "rigged"'.

catalysts.title: Post-election government formation in Israel
catalysts.description: Negotiations and coalition-building after historic vote with no clear winner, determining wartime leadership and policy direction.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'No clear winner in Israeli parliamentary election', 'Israelis go to the polls', 'Netanyahu's wartime leadership on the line'.

catalysts.title: Risk of security escalation tied to Israeli vote
catalysts.description: Calls for West Bank lockdowns, talk of restarting operations and high tensions during voting could trigger sudden security incidents.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Netanyahu Calls for West Bank Lockdown After Deadly Attack', 'Netanyahu made plans to restart Iran strikes earlier this month', 'Palestinians protest against military demolitions'.

catalysts.title: Transition to student-backed government in Serbia
catalysts.description: Student List's unexpected victory requires governance transition that may trigger protests, institutional challenges and regional diplomatic effects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Serbia’s ex-president Vučić concedes defeat to Student List', 'Protesters enter Serbian pro-Vucic TV station'.

catalysts.title: Return of opposition leader María Corina Machado
catalysts.description: Machado's homecoming could catalyse opposition mobilization and protests against the government amid external political ties.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returns to Venezuela', 'Now home, Venezuela opposition leader Machado walks tightrope'.

catalysts.title: New Zealand national election (Nov 7, 2026)
catalysts.description: National vote with early voting already open; outcomes will affect regional political narratives and turnout momentum.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Early voting opens in New Zealand for November 7 election with no clear frontrunner'.

catalysts.title: Bulgaria presidential runoff
catalysts.description: Close first-round vote moves to runoff, raising near-term electoral uncertainty and potential protests.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Bulgaria heads to presidential runoff after close vote'.
